(a) Equal Value Exchange.—The value of the Federal land and non-Federal land—
        (1) shall be equal; or 
        (2) shall be made equal in accordance with subsection (c).  
    (b) Appraisals.—The value of the Federal land and non-Federal land shall be determined by the Secretary through appraisals conducted in accordance with—
        (1) the Uniform Appraisal Standards for Federal Land Acquisitions; 
        (2) the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice; and 
        (3) Forest Service appraisal instructions.  
    (c) Equalization of Values.—
        (1) Surplus of non-federal land.—If the final appraised value of the non-Federal land exceeds the final appraised value of the Federal land, the County shall donate to the United States the excess value of the non-Federal land, which shall be considered to be a donation for all purposes of law. 
        (2) Surplus of federal land.—
            (A) In general.—If the final appraised value of the Federal land exceeds the final appraised value of the non-Federal land, the value of the Federal land and non-Federal land may, as the Secretary and the County determine to be appropriate, be equalized by the County—
                (i) making a cash equalization payment to the Secretary; 
                (ii) conveying to the Secretary certain land located in the County, comprising approximately 160 acres,
 as generally depicted on the map entitled “Sellar Park Parcel” and dated August 2004; or 
                (iii) using a combination of the methods described in clauses (i) and (ii).  
            (B) Disposition and use of proceeds.—
                (i) Disposition of proceeds.—Any cash equalization payment received by the Secretary under clause (i) or (iii) of subparagraph (A) shall be deposited in the fund established by Public Law 90–171 (commonly known as the “Sisk Act”) (16 U.S.C. 484a). 
                (ii) Use of proceeds.—Amounts deposited under clause (i) shall be available to the Secretary, without further appropriation, for the acquisition of land or interests in land in Colorado for addition to the National Forest System.    
    (d) Conditions on Certain Conveyances.—
        (1) Conditions on conveyance of crystal river parcel.—
            (A) In general.—As a condition of the conveyance of the parcel of Federal land described in section 3(3)(C) to the County, the County shall agree to—
                (i) provide for public access to the parcel; and 
                (ii) require that the parcel shall be used only for recreational, fish and wildlife conservation, and public open space purposes.  
            (B) Reversion.—At the option of the Secretary of the Interior, the parcel of land described in section 3(3)(C) shall revert to the United States if the parcel is used for a purpose other than a purpose described in subparagraph (A)(ii).  
        (2) Conditions on conveyance of wildwood parcel.—In the deed of conveyance for the parcel of Federal land described in section 3(3)(A) to the County, the Secretary shall, as determined to be appropriate by the Secretary, in consultation with the County, reserve to the United States a permanent easement for the location, construction, and public use of the East of Aspen Trail.

fable.w: The Secretary must consult with the County, a local government outside the federal government, before making the federal decision on reserving a permanent easement in the deed. The section also has the Secretary and the County jointly determine how values are equalized. The tempting reading is that this is only a land-exchange transaction with a counterparty, like an application or contract, but the text expressly requires consultation with a non-federal entity on a federal determination, which crosses the federal boundary.
fable.s: the Secretary shall, as determined to be appropriate by the Secretary, in consultation with the County, reserve to the United States a permanent easement for the location, construction, and public use of the East of Aspen Trail.

opus.w: Before deciding what easement the United States keeps in the deed for the Wildwood parcel, the Secretary must consult the County, a local government outside the federal government. Subsection (c)(2)(A) also requires a joint decision by the Secretary and the County on how to equalize the land values. It is tempting to treat the County as just the other side of a deal, like an applicant, but the statute requires consultation with a local government before a federal decision, and that crosses the federal boundary.
opus.s: the Secretary shall, as determined to be appropriate by the Secretary, in consultation with the County, reserve to the United States a permanent easement for the location, construction, and public use of the East of Aspen Trail.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting wrong reading:** This looks like a routine land-exchange deal where the County is just the other party to the transaction, much like an applicant or contractor, so it wouldn't count as participation. That reading fails because subsection (d)(2) requires the Secretary to consult the County before deciding on a federal action: the terms of the easement the United States keeps in the deed. A county is a local government, which is outside the federal government. This is the same kind of consultation as Example 2, where the Secretary had to consult state and local agencies and tribes before acting.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary to consult with the County (a local government entity outside the federal government) before reserving a permanent easement. This consultation with an outside party before a federal action (the reservation of the easement) constitutes participation under the definition.
qwen_chat.s: In the deed of conveyance for the parcel of Federal land described in section 3(3)(A) to the County, the Secretary shall, as determined to be appropriate by the Secretary, in consultation with the County, reserve to the United States a permanent easement for the location, construction, and public use of the East of Aspen Trail.
qwen_chat.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the phrase "in consultation with the County" in subsection (d)(2) constitutes participation because it involves an outside entity (the County). However, this consultation is regarding the specific terms of a land conveyance deed (an easement), which is essentially a bilateral agreement or contract between the government and the county, rather than a broader public participation process like a comment period, public hearing, or advisory board for a regulatory decision. More importantly, the primary mechanism described is the exchange of land and cash, which falls under the "applications for benefits or grants" or general administrative transaction trap, although here it is a specific statutory authorization for a swap. The consultation is limited to the technical details of the easement. Let's look closer. Is there any other participation? No public comment, no advisory board with outside members, no right to sue. The consultation is between the Secretary and the County. While the County is outside the federal government, is this "consultation... before making a decision"? The decision is to convey land. The consultation is about the easement. This is a specific negotiated transaction. The definition says "Participation is when the federal government may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government before making a decision." It also lists "consultation or coordination with states, tribes, local governments... before a federal action". This fits. The Secretary consults with the County before reserving the easement. This is a federal action (reserving an easement). So it is participation.

Wait, let's re-read the "No" traps. "applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses - applying for something is not participating in the decision". This is a land exchange authorized by statute. It's not an application. It's a specific transaction. The consultation is required. "The Secretary shall... in consultation with the County, reserve...". This is coordination with a local government before a federal action (reserving the easement). This fits the definition of participation.

Let's double check if "consultation with the County" is just intra-governmental? No, County is local government, which is outside.

Is it a "trap"? The trap is "consultation or coordination BETWEEN federal agencies". This is between a federal agency and a county. So it is not that trap.

Is it an "application"? No.

So, is it participation? Yes. The Secretary must consult with the County (outside entity) before reserving the easement (federal decision/action).
